difficulty.why: Level 4. The symptom is a chat feature failing in the renderer; the cause is the main process deciding, per Electron permission request, whether the requesting frame belongs to a VS Code window. An auxiliary window is opened at `about:blank`, so the requesting URL does not carry the workbench origin the check keys on, and it is denied. Reaching that means understanding how a window is created and what identity it carries afterwards — a relationship between two processes, with no identifier in the report to look up.

notes: The furthest symptom-to-cause distance in the pool. Everything the report offers — dictation, chat, `getUserMedia`, `NotAllowedError` — points at speech code, and the answer is in `code/electron-main`, a project nothing else in the pool touches. The failure mode this measures is an agent spending its turns in the subsystem the report named.
title: Speech-to-text fails with NotAllowedError: Permission denied in auxiliary (floating) chat windows
body:
Type: Bug Microphone / speech-to-text works correctly in the main VS Code window, but fails immediately when the same chat is opened in an auxiliary (floating) window. Steps to reproduce: Open a Copilot Chat in the main VS Code window. Start speech-to-text (dictation) — works fine. Right-click the chat → Move into New Window (auxiliary window). Start speech-to-text in the floating window. An error appears at the bottom of the window: Expected: Microphone permission granted to the session should apply to auxiliary windows, so speech-to-text works there too. Actual: getUserMedia is rejected with NotAllowedError: Permission denied in the auxiliary window only. The main window continues to work. Regression: This started ~2–3 days ago after a VS Code update. It was not an issue before. Notes / observations: Only auxiliary/floating windows are affected; docked chat in the primary window works. Windows OS-level microphone permission is enabled for desktop apps (main window confirms the mic is accessible). Appears to be that the auxiliary window is a separate Chromium browser context and does not inherit the microphone permission grant from the primary window.
